title: Write A Memo
equation: Decision Clarity = Written Thinking × Shared Context × Reduced Ambiguity
hook: That meeting went in circles because nobody wrote down what was actually being decided.
statement: Write important decisions down before you discuss them, so everyone shows up clear instead of emotional or confused.
explainer: A memo makes people say what they mean, what facts they're using, what they recommend, and what could go wrong. Without one, teams argue over fragments. With one, everyone starts on the same page.
sop: Name the decision in one line.
Write the context, facts, and options.
Send the memo before the meeting.
Decide only after everyone's read it.
equation_example: Written Thinking 8, Shared Context 7, Reduced Ambiguity 6. 8 × 7 × 6 = 336 Decision Clarity, out of 1,000. Higher means the room actually lands on a decision. Lower means the same debate comes back next quarter.
question: Pick one decision in your business and write a one-page memo before you talk about it again.
closing_statement: Think in writing before you decide out loud.
caption:
Principle Nº 258: Write A Memo

That meeting went in circles because nobody wrote down what was actually being decided.

Write important decisions down before you discuss them, so everyone shows up clear instead of emotional or confused.

Your turn: Pick one decision in your business and write a one-page memo before you talk about it again.
